verification.title: Build verification: September 23, 2026
verification.summary: 57 of 57 automated checks pass locally after the September 23 changes (including disturbances changed during a run: timing, exact replay from the saved scenario, no platform jump, the desktop panel and the web API) (designation, target names, shapes and sizes, scenario check, input validation), the fixes from an independent review (FPS metric, fast targets, coasting guard, faint-path speed, Benchmark 2 ground truth) and the fixes the PS audit led to (no derivative term, figure-8 sway within its setting, faint-track guards). The PS audit (tools/ps_audit.py) measures every PS item by running the code: 38 of 39 pass; Deliverable 1 fails because the check still expects macOS in the build workflow, which now builds Windows and Linux only (macOS through tools/build_macos.sh). The earlier suite (22 of 22) passed on Windows, Linux, macOS Intel and macOS Apple silicon runners on September 22, and each desktop archive was extracted and run on its own platform; the four-platform run will be repeated for this change. The web app ran a full scenario through the public site with report, CSV and summary downloads. Every PS row, shall item and deliverable re-read against 26169.pdf. The platform-maximum limit was re-measured at the allowed 10 deg/s and the faint beacon over ten seeds; both results are recorded as measured.
verification.note: Statuses are from runs in the repository, on GitHub Actions runners, and on the project server. Numbers quoted are measured, not estimated. Left for the team, not for the software: a hand-driven GUI session on a Windows and a Linux machine, a rehearsal of the 10 to 15 minute demo script, and, optionally, a narrated screen recording. Evaluator-supplied files arrive at the event; the template scenario and the video path are ready.

checks.name: Automated tests
checks.text: 45 of 45 pytest checks locally: geometry, gimbal limits, every path on screen and deterministic (seven kinds incl. user-defined waypoints), centroid accuracy, IMM prediction, closed loop clear, closed loop with vibration, identity under decoys, video path, PS rows 1 to 25 point by point, and 8 target tests (width and height, every shape, clamping and PS-envelope notes, physical-limit note, percent display, identical extra targets, the designated target is the one scored, identical decoys need a cue, typed start), and 5 review-fix tests (FPS is frames over processing time, a 4 deg/s target is kept centred, a coasting estimate cannot run off the screen, video ground truth gives errors, the CNN model is found from any folder), and 3 PS-audit tests (a still beacon is centred without oscillation, the platform sway never exceeds the set speed, a faint track is not walked off by noise). The earlier 22 passed on the Windows, Linux, Intel Mac and Apple silicon runners; that run will be repeated for the new tests.

checks.name: Scenario pack
checks.text: 16 scenarios (incl. the platform maximum at 10 deg/s and fast_circular), 15 s each, seeds 0 to 2, compared run by run with the previous batch. After the PS audit fixes, against the previous commit: 0 worse, 5 better by the tool's lock rule (platform maximum lock), every other run in its "same" band, although tracking errors dropped by about two thirds (the comparison tool flags error increases, not decreases). Clear line, circle and figure of 8: acquisition 0.60 to 1.33 s, 2.1 to 3.7 px mean tracking error, 100% lock, centroid error 0.006 to 0.007 px, 190 to 216 FPS. Clear random walk: 0.67 to 1.03 s, 5.1 to 6.3 px, 100%. Heavy noise (10% salt and pepper, sigma 20, Poisson): 0.67 to 1.00 s, 2.4 to 3.7 px, 100%, centroid 0.19 px, 97 to 105 FPS. Fog and low light: 0.63 to 1.57 s, 2.5 to 3.7 px, 100%, centroid 0.08 to 0.15 px. Faint beacon over seeds 0 to 9: 0.80 to 2.00 s, 2.4 to 3.5 px, 94.0 to 97.8% lock; seeds 7 and 8 at 94.8 and 94.0%, just above the 5% target-loss limit. Multi-target stress: 0.30 to 1.03 s, 10.3 to 11.3 px, 98.2 to 100% lock. decoys_identical: 3.3 to 3.5 px, 100%. beacon_shapes: 2.6 to 3.1 px, 100%. fast_circular (450 px circle at 4 deg/s, 80% of the turn rate): 0.67 to 0.70 s, 4.6 to 5.3 px, 100%. Hard mode: 2.83 to 11.97 s (search, by design), 2.6 to 3.7 px, 100%. FPS over the whole pack 69 to 216.

checks.name: Multi-seed envelope
checks.text: 3 seeds per scenario, all 13 scenarios of the September 22 pack; the faint scenario over 10 seeds. Clear, noise, fog, low light and faint pass every seed. The multi-target stress seed that swapped to a decoy now holds 98.8% lock at 14 px (candidates ranked by fitted width, which does not move with the noise level). Platform sway at the PS maximum held 76 to 88% lock at 5 and at 10 deg/s alike; after the review fixes 88.5 to 94.8%; after the PS audit fixes 93.4 to 97.2%, error 21.7 to 23.5 px: the random per-frame vibration is the physical limit.

checks.name: Truth independence
checks.text: The same random-motion run twice, the second time with ground truth deleted before the tracker: 0.000000 px difference in estimates and 0 px in the camera path over 240 frames. The tracker sees only the picture.

checks.name: Benchmark 2 path
checks.text: A synthetic 1200 x 1200 mp4 through the video input: 180 frames, lock 100%, CSV and PDF written. A 60 fps phone video tracked 669 of 754 frames with the 5 deg/s gimbal saturated 60% of the time. A ground-truth CSV (frame or t, x, y) now gives tracking error, centroiding error, RMSE and true lock for a video: on a noisy_line clip rendered to .mp4 with its truth, 8.09 px tracking and 0.188 px centroiding error; without it, n/a.

checks.name: Standalone executable
checks.text: Four native archives from one workflow: Windows x64, Linux x64 (Ubuntu 22.04 glibc), macOS Intel, macOS Apple silicon. On each platform's own runner the archive was extracted fresh and the executable ran clear line, full stress and video mode, wrote report, CSV and summary, and the GUI stayed alive for 12 s: Windows 77/52/113 FPS, Linux 76/61/105 FPS, Intel Mac 76/41/87 FPS, Apple silicon 176/82/258 FPS, identical tracking numbers on all four. Both macOS archives repeated by hand on a Mac (Apple silicon native 238/108/367 FPS, Intel under Rosetta 2 174/115/236 FPS). The served archives are byte-identical to the tested ones.

checks.name: AI detector
checks.text: Kept as a gap-filling fallback (v2, 8 px validation localisation, 51% of measurements on a phone video, 0% in the standard scenarios). The faint-beacon case it was meant for is now handled classically by track-before-detect, so nothing in the specification depends on the network. It is not used while a faint track is active: it was trained on visible beacons, and on a 3 to 6 sigma patch its peak was often noise. The model path is also looked up from the package folder, so an installed command started from another folder still loads it.

checks.name: Platform at PS maximum
checks.text: 20 px per frame sway plus 20 px per frame vibration: 93.4 to 97.2% lock (platform_max and platform_max_10degs, 15 s, seeds 0 to 2; 76 to 88% on September 22, 88.5 to 94.8% after the review fixes), error 21.7 to 23.5 px, acquisition 0.73 to 0.97 s. Measured with the gimbal at the 10 deg/s the PS allows (platform_max_10degs.yaml): slew saturation drops from about a third of frames to 2%, lock and error do not improve. So the motor is not the limit; the random per-frame vibration is, and no controller can anticipate a random jump before the frame arrives. Every report under vibration prints this in words beside the vibration-removed figure.

checks.name: Demo video
checks.text: About four minutes, composed by tools/make_demo_video.py from the engine's own frames: title cards, eight scenarios with scene view, camera view and live specification tiles, a Benchmark 2 segment on a video file, and a results card. On the site under downloads. A 10 to 15 minute live demo script is in docs/DEMO_SCRIPT.md.

checks.name: Web app on the server
checks.text: Same engine served by FastAPI behind Caddy on a 4-core ARM server: clear line 123 FPS, full stress 59 FPS there. A noisy-line run through the public site in a real browser locked at 1.43 s, 68 FPS, 5 of 5 specification checks, report and CSV downloaded. One run at a time, any number of viewers, reconnect on socket drop.

checks.name: PS re-read
checks.text: 26169.pdf re-read on September 20: rows 1 to 25, the eight shall items, five deliverables, four evaluation stages. All mandatory items implemented and tested. Optional items: colour camera, multiple targets, spiral, sinusoidal and user-defined (waypoint) paths, all disturbance kinds. Only the optional demo video is not produced.

checks.name: Frame-rate independence
checks.text: The estimator-lag compensation was set in seconds but the filter delay is a number of frames, so at camera rates above 30 Hz (the PS makes the rate user-defined, 30 Hz minimum) the controller over-led the target. It now scales with the update rate. At 60 Hz the stress scenario went from 15% to 94% lock; at 30 Hz every scenario reproduces its previous numbers exactly. Confirmed on the full pack: 36 of 36 runs unchanged against the previous batch, none worse.

checks.name: Tracked rate metric
checks.text: Every report, results dialog, web finish panel and command-line summary now prints the tracked rate (share of frames in TRACK) beside lock retention (TRACK and centred within 30 px). High tracked with low lock tells a reader the camera could not keep up, not that the beacon was lost. No definition changed.

checks.name: Desktop interface pass
checks.text: Interface reviewed from screenshots at 1600 x 1000 and 1366 x 768. Fixed: camera view turning the sky white near the screen edge (contrast stretch counted the off-screen area), overlapping legend and cut-off HUD lines, plot legends over the data, meaningless idle axes, misaligned form columns, tiles keeping live values after a run instead of the report's numbers, spurious picture-shift readout, a stray scrollbar artefact, a font warning on start, the simulator button active with no video, and an empty-legend warning in video reports. Native system fonts and one widget style on every platform.

checks.name: Desktop and web are one interface
checks.text: Both front ends are generated from fsoc_tracker/ui_shared.py: the panel (every field in the same sections, labels, tooltips and ranges), the six tiles and their pass rules, the telemetry lines, the view captions, the end-of-run summary, help and welcome text, decoy generation and the camera contrast stretch. The web page has the desktop toolbar with Pause, Step, Save scenario, Screenshot, Results, Manual and About, all four plots and the same keys. Verified in Chrome: a full run with pause, one-frame step, resume and stop, a video run, and the return to the simulator. Remaining differences are the server's: views sent at about 15 fps, one run per server, files downloaded rather than opened.

checks.name: Designated target (PS row 8)
checks.text: The tracker follows targets[designated] and the report scores it. Designation by appearance, by a start cue (as an operator or GPS cue would give) or by a point (a click on the preview or a video's first frame, or typed). Identical decoys starting apart, appearance only (20 s, seeds 0 to 4): the designated beacon was acquired in 1 of 5 runs and never in 3. With the start cue: 5 of 5 pass, acquisition 0.60 to 0.73 s, 5.7 to 6.6 px, 100% lock. Limit: look-alikes that start at the same point cannot be told apart at the start; even with the start cue those runs held 8 to 25% lock. Tracking every beacon at once was dropped as not required.

checks.name: Scenario check and input validation
checks.text: Every numeric input is clamped in the engine for every front end, and the scenario check notes Corrected values, values Beyond the PS (row named), settings Near the limit (the designated beacon above 70% of the turn rate: it can be done, with little margin; this was labelled Cannot be met before) and what Cannot be met (physical limits). Root cause of a failed web-app test: salt and pepper 13 (meant as 13%) was taken as a fraction and every pixel went black, so the beacon was never acquired. With 0.13 the same settings give acquisition 1.40 s, 99.4% lock, 11.9 px (above 10 px because jitter 10, turbulence 0.92 and 13% salt and pepper exceed the PS). Salt and pepper is now shown in percent on both panels.

checks.name: Tracker search fix
checks.text: While searching, candidates were re-measured on the last tracked frame's picture after a loss, or on no picture at all when several strong candidates appeared before the first lock (a crash, exposed by 50% salt and pepper). Now they are re-measured on the current frame. The regression batch is unchanged. Benchmark 2 sample video after the changes: acquisition 0.70 s, lock 100%, 194 FPS.

checks.name: Review findings
checks.text: An independent review by a teammate's session, answered with measurements. FPS was the mean of per-frame rates (faint seed 2, 30 s: 92.0 said, 67.8 true); now frames over processing time, the old value kept as fps_inst_mean for comparison only. Fast targets: the estimator was within 0.4 to 0.7 px of the truth; the controller's straight-line lead pointed off a tight curve; the lead is now capped at a 0.1 rad turn (450 px circle at 4 deg/s: 34.3 px, 14 to 19% lock before; 8.4 px, 100% after). A coasting estimate could run far off the screen (faint seed 2, 30 s: 158 px, 75.1% lock, 4.53 s re-acquisition); it now falls back to a whole-scene search (5.9 px, 96.2%, 0.07 s). Faint-path linking vectorised: 99th-percentile frame 149 to 160 ms to 26 to 33 ms. Read and shot noise now use independent random planes. Unchanged by design: the tracker observes the whole scene (the documented reading of the PS; a wide-field finder remains future work), and the CNN stays a gap filler. Not reproduced: a 5 px beacon in rain with 10% salt and pepper reported as never acquired; our run (figure of 8, 30 s, seeds 0 to 2) acquired in 0.77 to 1.37 s at 6.0 to 6.5 px, 100% lock, 86 to 99 FPS.

checks.name: PS audit
checks.text: tools/ps_audit.py measures every PS item by running the code: rows 1 to 25, the eight shall functions, the five deliverables, Benchmark 1, and Benchmark 2 with a rendered noisy video and its truth CSV. It writes docs/PS_AUDIT.md and exits with 1 if any check fails; the build workflow runs it on the Linux job, and it is in CONTRIBUTING.md and the pull-request template. 39 of 39 pass. It found three defects, all fixed. Shall 6: the derivative gain (kd 0.3) acted on an error that reaches the controller one frame late and in whole pixels, and drove a limit cycle of about +/-10 px; a still beacon was never settled (mean 6.4 px, peak 15.6 px). With kd 0 it is held within 4 px (mean 1.6 px); the integral term stays. Row 25: the figure-8 sway peaked at 28.3 px/frame when set to 20 (it is fastest at its crossing, sqrt(2) times the circle speed); it is now scaled so its peak equals the setting. Faint beacon seed 7: the sub-pixel refit slid onto noise clumps and the track walked off (86 px, 78.6% lock); the raw detection is now kept when the refit moves more than 3 px or the width exceeds 2.5 times the track's recent median, much wider candidates are not associated, and the CNN is not used on a faint track: 2.8 px, 94.8% lock.

checks.name: Archive rebuild
checks.text: The macOS Intel and Apple silicon archives on the site were rebuilt on 2026-09-23 from the current code (tools/build_macos.sh, same checks). The Windows and Linux archives predate the evening fixes and will be rebuilt by the workflow once an Actions budget is set or the free minutes reset.
